correctness.rationale: The genus-three smoothness discriminant Delta(s,u)=(s^2-4u)(u^2+u+3s^2+2) is the symmetric transform of (a-b)^2(a^2-4)(b^2-4) over F7. The curve has commuting involutions x->-x and x->1/x, giving three explicit genus-one quotients E0,E-,E+; the character-idempotent correspondence yields a 2-power, hence 7-prime, isogeny from their product to Jac(C), preserving p-rank and a-number. For each elliptic quartic y^2=f(x), supersingularity equals vanishing of the x^6 coefficient of f(x)^3. Independent symbolic symmetric expansion verified all three Hasse factors H0,H-,H+ mod7. Consequently each zero contributes (0,1) and each nonzero factor contributes (1,0), giving (3-r,r). Independent resultants in F7[s] and specialized gcd factorization of pairwise Hasse curves found precisely three smooth intersections for each pair, union of seven geometric points (six pairwise and one triple). All relevant gcds split linearly over F7 and no nonrational geometric roots remain; gradient determinants are nonzero. The fresh F7 check found 12,12,6,1 smooth (s,u) with a=0,1,2,3. This is an all-algebraic-closure statement deduced from elimination, not a conclusion from F7 enumeration.

originality.rationale: The positive-sign form y^2=(x^4+a x^2+1)(x^4+b x^2+1) equals Ohashi’s negative-sign standard form under parameter substitutions a->-a,b->-b. The exact object must be compared as Howe curves with Klein-four elliptic-quotient decomposition; all three elliptic Hasse invariants determine the p-divisible group, not just one direct Cartier rank. Ohashi’s all-p characteristic superspecial maximality theorem is broader in characteristic but narrower in invariant/focus. Borówka–Shatsila’s genus-three involution/Prym results cover quotient geometry in characteristic zero, not finite-characteristic Hasse-stratum intersections. General Hasse–Witt theory makes the calculation possible but does not give the six component equations or seven multiple intersections. Prior quotient isogenies imply that a-number is determined by three elliptic factors, but not where each factor is supersingular on this parameter plane or which nonordinary components meet. The new exact factors and geometric-elimination argument are necessary to derive the six rational irreducible components and exhaustive seven-point intersections.
